Ferrari NV Announces Multi-Million Euro Expansion in the Netherlands

Ferrari NV has unveiled plans to significantly expand its operations in the Netherlands, committing to a multi-million euro investment aimed at boosting its presence in the region’s thriving automotive industry. The announcement was made on Tuesday at the company’s Dutch headquarters in Zaltbommel, Gelderland, and was attended by local officials and industry representatives.

The expansion will see Ferrari NV increase its research and development capacities, as well as enhance its distribution network across the Benelux area. According to the company, the investment is expected to create up to 120 new skilled jobs over the next two years, ranging from engineering roles to logistics and customer support positions.

“We are proud to reinforce our commitment to the Netherlands, a country with a strong tradition in innovation and sustainability within the automotive sector,” said Luca Mariani, general manager of Ferrari NV’s Dutch division. “This expansion reflects both the growing demand for high-performance vehicles and our confidence in the local talent pool.”

The investment includes the construction of a new 8,000-square-metre facility adjacent to the existing site in Zaltbommel, which will house advanced testing laboratories and a training centre. Mariani emphasized that the new facility will help Ferrari NV stay at the forefront of technological developments, particularly in electric and hybrid drivetrains.

Local officials have welcomed the announcement. Marije van Dijk, alderman for Economic Affairs in Zaltbommel, commented: “This is a major boost for our region. Ferrari NV’s investment will not only generate jobs but also strengthen Gelderland’s reputation as a hub for automotive innovation.”

Industry analysts note that the move positions Ferrari NV to better serve the growing demand for sustainable mobility solutions in Western Europe. “With this expansion, Ferrari NV is responding to changing consumer preferences and stricter environmental regulations,” said Pieter Schouten, an automotive industry analyst at the Dutch Mobility Institute. “It is a strategic step that aligns with broader trends in the sector.”

The Netherlands Automotive Association (NAA) also expressed its support. NAA spokesperson Martijn Dekker stated, “We are pleased to see a renowned company like Ferrari NV deepening its roots here. Investments like these contribute to the continued vitality and competitiveness of our automotive landscape.”

Construction of the new facility is expected to begin in the third quarter of this year, with completion slated for late 2025. Ferrari NV has indicated that it will collaborate with local suppliers and educational institutions to maximize regional benefits.

The company reaffirmed its commitment to sustainability, noting that the new site will incorporate energy-efficient technologies and green building materials as part of its long-term strategy.
